name: archive_probe
description: Say what an archive or a document shows about its own protection, and what it does not. ZIP: structural, read by this tool from the bytes: the End Of Central Directory record (the one whose comment ends the file; another sound End record, in a comment, after the archive, or of an archive that lies wholly before the one that ends the file (a second archive appended; looked for in the last 64 KiB), is named, the answer is partial and protected is not false; the file is accounted for byte by byte: each member takes the bytes its local header and the directory's compressed size give it (and its data descriptor), the directory, the Zip64 records and the End record with its comment take theirs, and every other byte is dark wherever it lies: in front of the first member, between two members, between the last member and the directory, behind the End record. Dark bytes are searched for anything shaped like an archive, whatever the directory says (a directory entry that names the first member of an archive in front moves nothing): a local header or a directory entry whose own sizes end where the next record of the format begins or where the region ends (no version, method or name length is looked at; a local header whose sizes are in a data descriptor, bit 3 of the flags with zero or Zip64 sizes in the header, is found by its descriptor, the 4-byte or the Zip64 kind with its signature, within 16 MiB after the header and 256 MiB in all, and one that is not found in that reach is dark_unsearched; a streaming writer that leaves the descriptor's signature out is not found; a RAR 4 main header is read whole whatever its size), an End record that fits the file and is not the empty one (a ZIP library holds that as a constant), a 7-Zip start header or a RAR block whose CRC is right. One found is archive_in_front, archive_in_gap or archive_behind, partial, protected not false, whatever shape the archive has (damaged or missing End record, local headers only); a self-extracting stub, one that holds the signatures as constants too, is none of these; a block between the last member and the directory that holds no archive (an APK signing block) or zero padding is accepted, because only archive shapes are searched for; members whose bytes overlap each other or the directory are partial; a search the clock or more than 20000 signatures cut short is dark_unsearched, also partial. Second reader: where 7-Zip is installed it is asked for a listing, whatever its exit code (it exits 2 on a header error and still lists), and Type, member count and encrypted count must equal what was read; another format, a different count, a listing that did not finish or output that is not one archive's is partial (cross_check.result is differs). A file it cannot open or reads as a program (a stub) is not compared (not_compared). Where 7-Zip is not installed there is no second reader: the answer rests on the structural account alone, cross_check.result says not_installed and status_basis says so, which makes a complete answer weaker than with 7-Zip, the Zip64 end record wherever a Zip64 locator sits before it (whatever the End record says, as zipfile follows it; extensible data after its 56 fixed bytes is allowed for, also behind a stub whose offsets were not adjusted; an End record that ends the file with a record in its comment that it cannot be checked against is named), the disk numbers of a split archive's last part (named as split_archive; the directory is read, the data of members on other parts is not), and each central directory entry (empty and self-extracting archives included): per-member encryption (bit 0 of the flags is compared with the member's local header, 30 bytes read at the offset the directory gives: a disagreement, or no local header there, is named in local_header_flags, the answer is partial and protected is not false), the WinZip AES extra field, DOS times with their raw words and no zone; a name that is not valid UTF-8 is shown escaped and does not hide the other members. 7-Zip: listed through the installed 7z (bounded, no password prompt, no wildcard expansion of the archive's name (-spd: a file called ?.7z lists itself and not its siblings); an output that is not the listing of one archive (a second member section, a stray line in a record, a repeated key), or a warning or error line anywhere in it, or an archive property such as Tail Size (data after the end of the archive), makes the answer partial and protected not false, and protected is false only of a listing 7-Zip finished: a listing that was cut by the clock says true or null; its message that it cannot open the archive without a password is believed only where the start header shows an encrypted header, and not from a line that echoes the file name; the format it read must be 7z and its physical size must cover the file (a 7z whose header it cannot open is read as whatever follows it, a ZIP for example: not_the_whole_7z, partial, and protected true where the start header shows an encrypted header); it is ended at the clock, on a signal and, on Linux, when the tool is killed, and on Linux the read of its listing ends within a short grace of 7z's own exit rather than waiting for a program 7z forked to let go of the pipe, which that program is then also ended for (by holding the pipe, whether or not the tool ever saw it start); on macOS a killed tool leaves its 7z, and a program 7z forked that outlives 7z without the tool being killed is not ended, there being no /proc to find it by) where there is one, giving the members, each one's encrypted flag and whether the header is encrypted; the start header is read and its checksums checked, and a byte search is kept as a hint only when 7z is absent or cannot read the file. RAR: identified, protection not determined. PDF and OLE/Office: a heuristic byte search for markers, reported with offsets, never as 'not encrypted' and never as a verdict (doc_structure, a tool of the reverse-engineering pack that this pack does not depend on, reads the PDF trailer's encryption dictionary and the Office encryption structures: look for it in the run's tool inventory). When `structure` names a doc_structure result file of the run, a PDF or OLE answer also carries `structure_reading` (the field names of its items are printed only when they are in a closed list of descriptive names; the others are counted as `other_fields_not_shown`): the result is read only if it lies inside the run's directory with no link on the way, is a regular file of at most 16 MiB, is JSON of doc_structure's shape (its tool and parser fields, a complete or partial status, an encryption_summary), describes a file of this one's size and name (doc_structure/1 does not record the file's hash, so the match is by size and name; a result that records a sha256 must match this file's), and is otherwise REJECTED with the reason and none of its content shown; an accepted result's reading (found true, false or null, its basis and a short summary of its items) is reported beside the byte search with its source named, and the byte search stays a heuristic with status partial: no marker is not 'not encrypted', and the reading is only as good as the result it was taken from. Whether member names are readable is a finding separate from whether the data is encrypted. Nothing is extracted. What is loaded is bounded by max_metadata_bytes whatever the file's own headers declare: a ZIP whose central directory is declared larger than the bound (in the End record or the Zip64 record), larger than the file, or with more entries than the bound holds at 46 bytes each is not listed and says so; the directory is read in blocks, so memory does not follow its size. A PDF or an OLE file is searched whole, in a linear pass (bytes_searched and search_complete say so), because a PDF's marker sits at its end. The tool has its own clock (max_seconds, default 100, below the timeout of 120): at it, or on SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP, it ends the 7z it started and answers once (status partial, or failed with interrupted true, exit 128 + the signal). The clock is read for every ZIP entry and every 7z header string, and every mapped part of a file is read through the descriptor before it is used; a read that has not returned five seconds after the clock (a file on a volume or share that is not available) ends the tool with one answer, status partial, exit 0. The stop is the clock's, not the work's: the timer stays armed while the answer is sealed, so an answer too large to seal in that time is replaced by the short partial one, and a page fault or a read that sits in the system (a dead share) cannot be ended until the call returns. Every answer carries status and status_basis. SENSITIVE: member names, 7-Zip header strings, the 7z diagnostics and the path are evidence text. A part of one shaped like an identifier or a secret (a run of 10 digits or more, letters and digits of 8 or more, grouped digits, a recovery password, password=... , user-info, vendor tokens) is replaced by a marker in the answer and in every file it names (names_withheld counts them), the rest of the name stays; a second check of the output replaces what the first let through and makes the answer partial. Withholding is by shape, measured on random draws per shape planted in a member name or path (rates, not guarantees). Printed whole in 0 of 1,000 draws: hexadecimal ids of 16, 32 and 64, numbers of 10 digits or more, recovery passwords written with dashes, spaces, dots, underscores, no separator or one to three of any other characters between the groups (an en dash, a comma, a colon, a pipe, a tab), also when the groups are cut at the separators of the path (123456-123456/123456-...), full-width, split by invisible characters, or with one decimal digit glued to the first or last group, AWS access key ids, password= and api_key: assignments, user-info, 4x4 groups of capitals and digits joined by - or ., letters and digits of 8, 9, 12, 16 or 40 characters that hold a capital, a small letter and a digit, and a full-width id. Printed whole in some draws: uniform draws of letters and digits (every character as likely a capital, a small letter or a digit as any other) of 8 characters about 2.5%, of 9 about 2%, of 12 about 1%, of 16 about 0.6%, of 24 at most 0.1% and of 40 none; random lowercase letters and digits of 8 about 7%, of 12 about 2.4%, of 16 about 0.4%; 24 random letters 1.5% to 2.6%; a 16-character base32 id 2.2% to 3.4% (by alphabet); four groups of four lowercase hexadecimal digits joined by underscores 4% to 9% (by how the draws are made); an id of 12 or 16 characters whose letters are half Cyrillic or Greek look-alikes about 1%. NOT recognised, by design, and printed whole: an identifier of 7 characters or fewer, a number of 9 digits or fewer, a lowercase-only run of up to 22 letters (it reads as a word), an all-capital letters-only run of any length, three groups of four or five capitals and digits joined by - or . (a rule for them would also withhold upper-case constants such as OpenSSL manual page names), a recovery password cut by anything other than a separator or with a letter in it or glued to it (the groups then show), a ten-digit number written 3-3-4, an e-mail-like lowercase string, and a secret of any other shape; a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true. What the rule is given is bounded: a string of more than 4096 characters (as written or after folding), a path of more than 8192, or a string with a / and a run of more than 256 name characters is withheld whole as '<text too long to judge withheld>' and not judged (the slowest string inside the bound that a search found took 0.13 CPU s). The output check, which reads every printed string once more, is narrower than the rule: with the rule removed it replaces recovery passwords (full-width ones too), AWS ids, password= values, PEM headers, user-info, hexadecimal of 16 digits or more and runs of 24 or more characters that flip between letters and digits, and it lets through numbers of 10 to 20 digits, ids of up to 23 characters, some base64 (about one in five of 32 bytes), every recovery password whose groups are joined by anything but a hyphen, underscore, dot, space or nothing, and every recovery password cut over the components of a path (the first layer alone holds those). The rule also changes names that are not secrets: of the file names of a documents tree 6.9% have a part withheld (10-digit timestamps, UUIDs) and 0.6% of its directories, of an application tree 16% and 3.1% (a word with a digit inside, such as libmp3lame, is withheld in part). A name, a path, a URL or a message that quotes a credential is withheld with the identifier-shaped strings, from version 14: a value given to a password, token, secret or cookie name (password=..., Pwd=..., a Cookie header), a Name/Value pair in text whose Name is a credential (a number, an array or a long Value too, and the NewValue after an OldValue), a -Password style switch, the argument of ConvertTo-SecureString, curl -u user:pass, mysql -uUSER -pSECRET, a bcrypt hash and the known token families; the text is replaced by a marker that holds only its length. Before, only identifier-shaped strings (tokens, key ids, user-info) were withheld, so these were printed. Known gaps: a pair whose Value is an array nested in another or longer than 4,096 characters, a crypt hash that is not bcrypt, and a secret that has neither a credential name nor a token shape. It reports what 7z printed on a pipe, so a host that cannot adopt orphans does not make an answer less than complete (`program_group` says so); a process 7z leaves behind is ended and the answer is `partial`, and a process that holds 7z's pipe after 7z ended (silently, or writing without end) is let go one second after 7z ended, with the listing `listed_with_warnings` and `pipe_held`. Every answer that is not a refusal or an error carries `program_group` (subreaper, left_behind, unproven, notes).

path.description: A ZIP, 7-Zip, RAR, PDF or OLE document

structure.description: Optional: the path, inside the run, of a doc_structure result file (a job reference to a PDF or OLE document's structural reading). Read for a PDF or OLE file only; validated before use, rejected with a reason when it is not doc_structure's, is for another file, or lies outside the run

limit.description: Members (or 7-Zip header strings) shown inline (default 200, at most 1000); all of them are counted, and when there are more the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in all_results

max_metadata_bytes.description: The most container metadata to load or search: a ZIP central directory, a 7-Zip header (default 33554432, at least 4096). A ZIP whose central directory is declared larger (in either end record), larger than the file, or with more entries than this holds at 46 bytes each is not listed and says so. It does not bound the search of a PDF or an OLE file, which is always whole

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds (default 100, 1 to 110; the manifest's timeout is 120). At it the 7z is ended and the answer says what was not read; a read that has not returned five seconds later ends the tool with one partial answer
